20921-adventures-in-the-arts-informal-ch:
True artists refuse to shelve life in one snug, fixed idea, argues Adventures in the Arts. Most folk, it says, lock life away young in a tidy mental box. Marsden Hartley's informal chapters on painters, vaudeville, and poets push back hard.

Hartley, a noted American painter, writes of art with a maker's frank eye. Studios, stages, circuses, and poems all feed his roving talk. He prizes fresh seeing over stock taste at every turn. The book gives readers a vivid, quirky tour of creative life in the 1920s, told by a man who lived it from inside.
22523-the-history-of-the-american-expedi:
Joel R. Moore, Harry H. Mead, and Lewis E. Jahns wrote the history of the American expedition fighting the Bolsheviki. American troops served in Russia after the First World War. Their own unit history opens with America's war declaration.

Congress declared a state of war with Imperial Germany, the document begins. That declaration set the chain of service in motion for these men. From training camps they shipped to a very different front. In north Russia they fought Bolshevik forces around Archangel. Cold, confusion, and an unclear mission marked that campaign. The veterans' history preserves orders, rosters, and memories in detail. It remains a key record of America's forgotten Russian intervention.
al-masudi-prairies-dor-meynard-vol-vi:
Tome six of the French al-Masudi came from Barbier de Meynard's hand in 1871. Les Prairies d'Or renders the Muruj al-Dhahab, the great tenth-century summa of the Baghdad traveler al-Masudi. The Société Asiatique printed the nine tomes between 1861 and 1877, with Pavet de Courteille sharing the labor.

The work treats the world whole. Its seas and rivers, its peoples and their kings, its faiths and its wonders all pass in review. The history of Islam follows, year by year. Al-Masudi reports marvels with a traveler's shrug and hard facts with a scholar's care. In French the book became Europe's fullest door into his mind. This tome is the sixth stretch of the road.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-boniface-vi: A 1913 entry on Boniface VI — the pope of the fifteen days. Thomas Oestereich records his brief reign. The entry preserves his modest fame. The stormy age chose and lost him. A pope of the ninth century. His election followed the Formosan storm.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ercole-consal: This 1913 reference piece on Cardinal Consalvi — the pope's great minister — praises his famous work. Francis Schaefer wrote it up. He made the 1801 pact with Napoleon. He stood firm at Fontainebleau. Rome loved its wise statesman. His 1801 concordat is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-henry-vi: A 1913 entry on Henry VI — the Hohenstaufen emperor. Franz Kampers unfolds his fateful reign. He claimed the Sicilian crown. The empire knew the youthful lord. The heir of the Barbarossa's might. His 1197 death is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-mondovi: Mondovì, the Piedmontese city beneath the Alps, has been a bishop's see since the 1300s. This entry covers its diocese, its cathedral, and its history at the foot of the mountains. The faith in the shadow of the Alps, where the bishops of Mondovì ruled a mountain diocese.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pierre-jean-o: Peter Olivi was the Franciscan theologian whose apocalyptic thought divided the order. This entry covers his career, his doctrines, and his condemnation. The prophet of the Spirituals: his radical poverty doctrine split the Franciscan order in two forever afterward in schism.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-adrian-v: Adrian VI was the Dutch reformer pope who confessed the Church's sins. This entry traces his pontificate, his austerity, and his lonely death. The last non-Italian till John Paul II: his lonely tomb lies in Rome's German Santa Maria dell'Anima.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-alexande: Alexander VI was the Borgia pope whose name became a byword. This long entry traces his pontificate, his children, and his legend. The most notorious of the Renaissance popes: his famous bull divided the whole New World between Spain and Portugal.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-benedict: Benedict VI was the pope strangled in the Castel Sant'Angelo. This entry traces his pontificate, his deposition, and his murder. The martyred pope of the Crescentii: his cruel murder stained the dark papal fortress forevermore in his innocent martyr's blood.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-clement-: Clement VI was the magnificent pope of Avignon's golden age and the Black Death. This entry traces his pontificate, his splendor, and his charity. The most worldly of the Avignon popes: his splendid court dazzled the visiting kings and queens.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-gregory-: Gregory VI was the pope who bought the tiara and resigned it at Sutri. This entry traces his pontificate, his simony, and his abdication. The pope who paid for Peter's keys: his humble resignation saved the coming reform at Sutri.

Gregory XVI was the Camaldolese pope who condemned liberalism's errors. This entry traces his pontificate, his encyclicals, and his conservatism. The last monk on the throne: his stern Mirari Vos condemned the liberal age outright and wholly in 1832's August.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-innocent: Innocent VI was the reforming pope of Avignon's sterner age. This entry traces his pontificate, his reforms, and his legate Albornoz. The austere restorer of the Papal States: his great legate reconquered papal Italy by the sword alone in war.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-john-vi: John VI was the Greek pope who faced the Lombard duke of Benevento. This entry traces his pontificate, his diplomacy, and his firmness. The peacemaker of the Lombard wars: his bold ransom saved the besieged Romans from Duke Gisulf's Lombards.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-john-xv-: This entry covers the pontificates of John XV and the antipope John XVI, the Greek intruder of 997. It traces their reigns, their fates, and the age's confusions. Two Johns of the dark century: one's nose was slit by the Romans.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-leo-vi: Leo VI was the pope of 928 whose seven months left barely a trace. This entry notes his brief pontificate and the scant records as the 1913 editors found them. A shadow of the tenth century: his months passed unnoticed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-pius-vi: Pius VI was the pope who died a French prisoner at Valence. This entry traces his pontificate, his humiliation, and his martyrdom. The pope of the Revolution's fury: his martyred corpse returned in triumph to Rome in 1802's cold winter.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-stephen-: Stephen VI was the pope of the Cadaver Synod's horror. This entry traces his pontificate, the trial of Formosus's corpse, and his lynching. The pope of the corpse's trial: his ghastly synod judged the rotting dead in 897's cold January.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-urban-vi: Urban VI was the pope whose election sparked the Great Schism. This entry traces his pontificate, his violence, and the divided Church. The pope of the schism's birth: his violent temper split the Western Church into two rival obediences in 1378.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-raymond-vi: Raymond VI of Toulouse was the count of the Albigensian wars. This entry traces his excommunication, his humiliation, and his end. The humbled lord of Languedoc: his public scourging pleased the papal legate at Saint-Gilles in 1209's hot June days.
doe-osti-1774872-american-made-challenge: Acoustic cleaving of gallium arsenide got its challenge report, and this American-Made CRADA text covers next-gen photovoltaics. The pages detail the cleaving method. The solar makers get their technique. The challenge was American-Made. The method was cleaving.
doe-osti-2997296-realizing-the-materials: Printing parts that fit their world got its DOE vision, and this report shows the new path. The pages detail the design approach. The manufacturers get their roadmap. The path was fundamentally different. The approach was design. The vision was DOE's.
doe-osti-2997456-high-power-fpc-progress: EIC's high-power couplers got their progress, and this DOE report covers FPC work for ESR cavities. The pages detail the advances. The collider builders get their update. The couplers were high power FPC. The cavities were ESR. The builders got updates.
doe-osti-3004275-radioisotope-science-an: Radioisotope R&D got its FY2025 summary, and this DOE division covers core projects. The pages detail the findings. The isotope folks get their record. The year was FY2025. The record was isotope. The projects were competitive. The summary was core.

doe-osti-3021636-development-of-high-thr: RNA mods got assay-developed, and this DOE text builds high-throughput in vitro. The pages detail the findings. The bio folks get their data. The assays were RNA modifications. The data were bio. The vitro was in. The RNA were assays.
doe-osti-3021932-effect-of-the-form-of-c: Chromium got HLW-vitrified, and this DOE text studies the form effects. The pages detail the findings. The nuclear folks get their data. The vitrification was HLW. The data were nuclear. The effects were form. The chromium was form. The HLW was vitrification.
doe-osti-3375617-extending-component-lif: Solar inverters — the boxes that turn panel DC into grid AC — fail far more often than the panels. The ECLAIIR project works on making these components last longer and fail less. Longer-lived inverters mean cheaper solar power for everyone.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIAMarchettiVic:
Victor Marchetti had been a high-ranking CIA officer, a special assistant near the top of the agency, before he became its most troublesome defector in print. Penthouse magazine framed its interview with him as an open letter to the CIA.

Marchetti talks about covert operations, including the destabilization of Chile, from inside knowledge of the building he had served. His book The CIA and the Cult of Intelligence had already made legal history through the government's effort to censor it before publication. The interview is preserved as part of the seventies exposure wave, when former officers became the agency's loudest critics.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MertzMichaelVic:
An unnamed writer addressed this letter to 'Bud' on April 15, 1980. Its subject is what the writer calls the heroin angle. The letter discusses reporter Les Payne and 'The Heroin Trail,' a newspaper investigation of the drug trade. It also mentions the French SDECE, that country's foreign intelligence service. The author's name cannot be recovered from the garbled scan.

Heroin trafficking threads run through assassination research of the period, linking Marseille, intelligence services, and exile politics in researchers' theories. This letter shows one reader working those connections in private correspondence. It names its sources and its suspicions, even if the file cannot name the man who wrote it down.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-OgilvieClaytonC: nsia-OgilvieClaytonCorrespondence Ogilvie Clayton Correspondence: the made public government document, captured as titled. Subject: government records. A bare file, kept as issued. An obscure item, complete. From the archive shelves, for readers of the files and readers.
nasa-tm-19640023414-mission-plan-tiros-v: The Aeronomy and Meteorology Division at Goddard Space Flight Center prepared this mission plan for the TIROS VI satellite. TIROS craft were America's early weather satellites, built to photograph clouds from orbit. A mission plan sets out a satellite's aims, orbit, and ground operations before flight. The hosted sample preserves only the plan's cover page, with no readable body text, so the plan's details cannot be described from the sample itself.
nasa-tm-19660007969-preliminary-results-:
Luther W Slifer Jr and Stephen G McCarron at Goddard reported early results in October 1965 from a solar cell test flown on Explorer XXVI. Different cell designs were mounted on the satellite. In orbit, radiation slowly damages solar cells and cuts their output. The experiment compares how well each design resisted that damage, the catalog note says.

Results are called preliminary, so the flight record was still short. Even early readings guide the choice of cells for later satellites. Power loss in orbit cannot be repaired after launch. A side-by-side test in real space was the surest way to learn which cell design aged most slowly.
nasa-tm-19700017984-space-manufacturing-:
Hans F. Wuenscher of the Marshall Space Flight Center wrote this report on July 11, 1969. It looks at kinds of manufacturing that only zero gravity makes possible. In orbit, melts and mixtures behave in ways they never do on Earth.

Without gravity, there is no sinking, rising, or settling in a cooling melt. Wuenscher surveys what could be made under those conditions. He treats factory work that the space setting itself enables, not work merely moved into space. Studies of this kind shaped early plans for space stations. They asked what products might one day justify building plants in orbit.
nasa-tm-19700026597-the-photoconductive-:
John J. Park of the Goddard Space Flight Center wrote this report in June 1970. It studies the light-sensitive layer inside AVCS-APT vidicon tubes. Vidicon tubes were the cameras that sent pictures from early weather and Earth-view satellites, so the quality of that layer set the quality of the pictures.

Park analyzes how selenium and sulfur amounts vary across layers on typical tube face plates. He also measures layer thickness and checks how the maker's own optical method skews those readings. Certain layers showed grain boundaries, a sign of an unacceptable light-sensitive coating. Electrical tests then trace how makeup and thickness changes affect performance, and point to a best thickness range.

podcast-joerogan-72P_9jmrOVI:
Ethnobotanist Dennis McKenna and Josh Wickerham join episode 477 of the Joe Rogan Experience. McKenna, brother of Terence, has studied plant medicines in the Amazon for decades. Wickerham works on sustainable sourcing of those same plants, and together they give the talk a field-work base.

They describe how Amazonian peoples use psychedelic plants in healing and ritual, and what science has confirmed so far. Rogan asks about the rush to commercialize these traditions and the harm it can do. The episode balances wonder with care, showing two experts who respect both the plants and the cultures that kept them.
podcast-joerogan-QHQzoHolWvI:
Comedian Theo Von joins Joe Rogan to tell how he tried ketamine therapy in a segment from the show. Von is a comic known for odd tales from a hard youth in the South. His drug tales mix pain with laughs.

Von tells what the clinic felt like, what the drug showed him, and what stuck when he came back. He weighs the help it gave his mood against the strangeness of the cure. Rogan asks the blunt bits his crowd wants to know. Listeners get a comic's frank take on a new cure. The library holds the segment as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-TyODZ4IjBVI:
Jason Silva, Duncan Trussell, and Ari Shaffir crowd into episode 369 of the Joe Rogan Experience, an early group session from the show's wild years. Silva is a futurist performer, Trussell the house mystic, and Shaffir a gleefully rude stand-up. Rogan hosts his friends like a party.

The talk spins through psychedelic tales and big ideas about tech and the mind, with Shaffir grounding every flight in a joke. No single subject owns the hour. The episode is a group portrait of Rogan's circle before fame sorted it, and a sample of the loose hang format the show grew from.
podcast-tuckercarlson-TSZXlVF-qVI:
Is there evidence of God in mathematics? Tucker Carlson takes up that question in a segment of his podcast. The claim is an old one in new dress: that the deep order of numbers, beautiful and unforced, points to a mind behind the world.

Carlson works through the argument with care, asking why math describes nature so well and whether chance can explain the fit. The talk speaks to his audience's wider interest in faith under pressure from a secular age. The segment is a short piece of popular theology, built on wonder at the strange fact that the universe can be read in numbers at all.
studies-in-the-life-of-the-christian-his: Henry T. Sell studies the Christian life — its faith and its service — in clear, practical lessons. His work guided Sunday schools for years. Sound, simple teaching for believers. Prayer, witness, and loving service are his three great themes. Teachers found his outlines a sure help in class.
un-doc-united-nations-special-committee-:
Partition takes detailed shape in Chapter VI of the 1947 report of the United Nations Special Committee on Palestine. A majority of the panel backed splitting the mandate into two states, one Jewish and one Arab. Jerusalem was to sit under international rule, outside both states.

The chapter draws the proposed borders and explains the economic union that would still link the two states. It covers citizenship, holy places, and the steps for British withdrawal. Months later the General Assembly adopted a partition plan much like this one, and its lines still echo today.
